speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Education with regard to the recent exam paper leak at an Institute of Higher Learning (IHL) (a) whether all IHLs have sufficient measures in place to prevent similar incidents from occurring; and (b) if so, what are these measures.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Education in view of the recent exam paper leak at an Institute of Higher Learning (IHL) (a) what measures are put in place by the IHLs to ensure that papers do not get leaked and are protected with secure confidentiality when students take the papers at multiple locations; and (b) what assistance is provided by the IHLs to students affected mentally with having to retake the exams in cases where papers are leaked.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Members have asked about the recent premature online release of a NTU test paper, what the root causes were and also whether all our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) have sufficient measures to prevent similar incidents from occurring.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: NTU is conducting an internal investigation into the leakage of a test paper that occurred earlier this month.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The individual had failed to password-protect the electronic version of the test paper which was meant for students taking the test online.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As a result, the students were inadvertently given access to the questions before the test started.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: NTU takes this matter seriously and is reviewing its internal protocol and staff training to prevent recurrence of a similar incident.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The IHLs acknowledge the additional stress on students when there is a need to retake examinations.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Sufficient time is provided for students to prepare for the re-examination.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: In addition, lecturers and mentors avail themselves to support affected students.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Students who require more assistance can also turn to para-counsellors or professional counsellors in the IHLs.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I declare that I am an academic staff at an IHL and clearly my concerns are for the students.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I share the Minister of State's concerns that this is an added stress for our students.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: She mentioned about allowing sufficient time, but I would like to ask the Ministry if it could prepare a standard set of guidelines for all our IHLs to adhere to, just in case this incident happens again.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This means the students has a standard time to prepare for the next make-up exam.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My second supplementary question is for the lecturers themselves.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I think one of the fears for us is when the exam papers leak, we need to prepare alternative papers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In this case, there could be instances where we need to prepare more.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Ministry provide assurance that we do not have to prepare too many alternatives in such incidents in the future?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Can I request Dr Wan Rizal to repeat the second supplementary question, please?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The Member mentioned that in some instances, the lecturers may have to prepare for several papers?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: One of the concerns that some of the lecturers shared with me is that we do already have to prepare make-up exam papers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: But with this incident occurring, there might be an occurrence where we need to prepare more and this is something that we are concerned about.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Ultimately, we have to understand the purpose of having examinations, assessments and tests.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: These are mainly to gauge the students' understanding of the topics that they have been taught and the ability to apply the knowledge that they have gained during the course of their lessons.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On guidelines for IHLs to adhere to and standardising the time for students to retake exams, I think we need to understand that there are different types of tests, exams and assessments for different disciplines as well as subjects.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Some may be covering many topics, some may be very few topics; for some tests, the students may need a lot of time to prepare, for some maybe modular in nature.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, it may not always be practical to prescribe a standard time for students to prepare for re-examination.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On the second point about the lecturers and the staff having to prepare for more make-up examination papers, I believe that our IHLs do work as a team, at the team level and not at the individual level.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And indeed, it is useful for each IHL to have its own system and also have some flexibility to prepare for not just the main exam, but also for contingencies.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have Clementi residents who are following the news of this.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And likewise, whether there were other processes to reduce the risk of one human error affecting an entire cohort of exam candidates?
